feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a fine line with Trump
entry.summary: A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

entry.title: Politics chat: Duffy calls for more funding, Democrats plans for accountability
entry.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.

entry.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
entry.summary: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

entry.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
entry.summary: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

entry.title: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal
entry.summary: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

entry.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
entry.summary: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

entry.title: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
entry.summary: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

entry.title: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
entry.summary: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

entry.title: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
entry.summary: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

entry.title: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.
